panels.visual: A huge Persian army marching along a coast with endless banners, King Xerxes on a golden chariot
panels.caption: In 480 BC the Persian king Xerxes invaded Greece with a huge army.

panels.visual: The narrow pass of Thermopylae between steep cliffs and the sea with a thin line of Spartan soldiers in red cloaks, round shields, King Leonidas in front
panels.caption: At the narrow pass, Leonidas with three hundred Spartans held them off for three days.

panels.visual: A Persian messenger demanding weapons, Leonidas replying calmly with his spear
panels.caption: Leonidas is said to have answered: come and take them.

panels.visual: A local man, Ephialtes, pointing at a mountain path behind the Greeks, Persian scouts creeping on the high trail, dusk; no violence shown
panels.caption: Ephialtes showed the Persians a path round behind them. The Persians then marched on and burnt Athens.
